summary.title: Neural Network OCR
summary.one_liner: Learn how to build a feed-forward neural network for letter recognition in C# and how to pick a good set of line-based "receptor" features using entropy.
keywords: how to recognize letters with a neural network
letter image to neural network input
takeaways: Letter images can be turned into bipolar (0.5 / -0.5) input vectors, with one output neuron per letter for training a backpropagation network.
A single-layer network with 30 inputs and 26 outputs can be trained to recognize 5x6 pixel capital letters, and recognition picks the output with the maximum value.
Line-based receptors that are either crossed or not crossed by a letter can replace pixel inputs, so large images need few input features.
Receptor usefulness is scored as OuterEntropy * (1 - AverageInnerEntropy), and the best ones are kept from a large random set (e.g. 500 down to 100).
The author reports the approach works on ideal fonts (0/26 and 0/130 misclassified) but hand-drawn letters give mixed results.
summary.summary: The article reviews neural network approaches to optical character recognition. It first describes a common method: a feed-forward network trained with backpropagation on bipolar-coded pixel vectors, with C# code using the AForge.NET library. It then proposes a second method that replaces pixels with randomly generated line "receptors", filtered by an entropy-based usability score. A companion test application is used to show training and misclassification results on regular and italic fonts. The author presents it as research, not a finished OCR solution, and notes limits such as the need for ideal training data.
